source_name: Institut sertifikovanih računovođa Crne Gore (ISRCG)
why_relevant: Self-regulatory professional body for certified accountants, auditors, valuers, internal auditors and forensic experts; it maintains member registries by category/title and applies ISA/IFRS/IVSC standards. Relevant to A3 because accounting/audit rule changes and reporting deadlines flow through it, and its registries are pointers to the adviser and audit-firm population serving banks.

source_name: Institut računovođa i revizora Crne Gore (IRRCG)
why_relevant: A second, separate accountancy/audit institute — the existence of competing professional bodies matters because it signals contested self-regulation and duplicated registries; both must be tracked to get full coverage of the audit/accounting profession advising banks.

source_name: Bankar.me — banking trade portal (association-coverage proxy)
why_relevant: Specialist banking portal that reports UBCG statements and lobbying positions — including concrete proposals such as the association's push on banking-secrecy access for courts, police and tax authorities. Because UBCG's own site publishes consultation responses only sporadically, this tag feed is often the fastest visible trace of an association position.

source_name: MINA / CdM economy desks — association statement wire (proxy for UBCG and UPCG positions)
why_relevant: National agency and portal coverage frequently carries the full text of association saopštenja that never appear on the associations' own sites — e.g. the 2026 UBCG assembly adopting a new Statute and a 2026-2031 financial framework, and its broadened remit into digitalisation/AI, ESG, AML/CFT and financial inclusion. Practical fallback channel for detecting association activity.

source_name: European Banking Federation — member/affiliate page for Montenegro
why_relevant: UBCG is an EBF affiliate member; EBF pages and position papers give an English-language, EU-benchmarked view of what the Montenegrin association is aligning to, and identify the EU files (payments, AML, ESG reporting) likely to be transposed next.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — registry profile of Udruženje banaka Crne Gore
why_relevant: Commercial registry aggregator giving the association's legal identity, registered address (Novaka Miloševa BB, Podgorica) and registration date (2003), plus officer data. Useful for entity resolution and for confirming legal form when the association's own site is thin — and the same aggregator can resolve every member bank and adviser found via the association directories.

source_name: NVOinfo — NGO registry entry for Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore
why_relevant: Montenegrin NGO directory; because most Montenegrin associations, institutes and professional bodies are registered as NGOs, this directory is a systematic pointer for discovering additional finance-adjacent associations and consumer bodies that do not surface in ordinary search.

source_name: gov.me public-consultation announcements (association response counterpart)
why_relevant: Not an association source itself, but the mandatory counterpart: each 'javna rasprava na Nacrt zakona' notice carries the consultation window and the address for comments, and the resulting report on the public discussion names which associations submitted positions. This is the reliable way to catch association consultation responses that are never published by the association.

source_name: CeJN – Centralni elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crne Gore (Portal javne nabavke, Tenderi)
why_relevant: Montenegro's single mandatory e-procurement portal: every contracting authority (CBCG, Ministarstvo finansija, Poreska uprava, Agencija za nadzor osiguranja, state-owned banks/post) must publish tender notices, tender documentation, award decisions and contract values here. This is the primary early-warning channel for supervisory IT systems, registries, payment infrastructure and core-banking/advisory procurements, typically 6-18 months before any policy announcement.

source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (former Uprava za javne nabavke) – Ministarstvo finansija
why_relevant: Policy owner and system operator for public procurement: publishes the legal framework, notices to economic operators, registration rules for the e-system, annual reports on procurement volumes, and methodological guidance. Useful as a pointer to which authorities procure what, and to changes in the rules that alter what becomes visible in CeJN.

source_name: Centralna banka Crne Gore (CBCG) – Tenderi i oglasi
why_relevant: The central bank's own tender/announcement page. CBCG is the single most important buyer in this cell: supervisory reporting systems, credit registry (Kreditni registar), RTGS/instant payments infrastructure, AML tooling, IT security and advisory. Its notices and plan javnih nabavki reveal budget, technical requirements and go-live deadlines for payment and supervisory infrastructure.

source_name: nabavke.com – Montenegrin tender aggregator and document mirror
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that mirrors CeJN notices and, critically, hosts the underlying PDF documents (e.g. 'Obavjestenje_o_ishodu_postupka' for CBCG contracts) on stable, easily fetchable URLs. Useful as a redundancy layer and for historical notices that the official portal may rotate out, and for named-authority browsing (e.g. Centralna banka Crne Gore, Pošta Crne Gore).

source_name: javne-nabavke.com – Montenegro tender monitoring service
why_relevant: Regional monitoring service that claims to track CeJN plus additional sources; publishes aggregate market statistics (annual notice counts, average estimated value, average bid preparation time) that are useful for sizing the Montenegrin public IT procurement market and for benchmarking deadlines.

source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki (successor of Državna komisija) – Rješenja
why_relevant: The procurement review body publishes rulings (rješenja) on bidder complaints. These reveal contested financial-sector IT tenders, disqualified/complaining vendors, technical specification disputes, and delays that push implementation deadlines — information not visible from the award notice alone. Also a strong pointer to the vendor ecosystem, since complainants are named.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Supplement to the Official Journal)
why_relevant: Publishes above-threshold notices including EU-funded (IPA) contracts and service/advisory contracts where the EU Delegation or EU bodies are the contracting authority for Montenegro. Machine-readable notices with CPV codes, estimated values, deadlines and awarded contractors; the canonical channel for EU-financed financial-sector technical assistance and IT.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) – notices
why_relevant: Since EBRD moved all client project procurement here, ECEPP is now the exclusive channel for procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract-award notices under EBRD-financed and EBRD-administered-grant projects in Montenegro — including financial-sector advisory, PIU support and IT for public bodies. Notices carry budget, TOR-level technical requirements and submission deadlines.

source_name: EBRD project procurement notices (ebrd.com) and corporate/consultancy procurement
why_relevant: The public-facing index that explains publication rules (Guidance note on Publication of Procurement Notices) and links through to ECEPP; the corporate procurement/consultancy pages cover EBRD's own consultant assignments, which for Montenegro often include banking-sector diagnostics, NPL work and payments advisory.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations – Montenegro project and procurement pages
why_relevant: World Bank project pages carry Project Appraisal Documents, Procurement Plans (STEP) and implementation status reports for Montenegro. Financial-sector operations (DPLs, financial sector strengthening, public finance management, revenue administration IT) disclose planned contract packages, methods and dates years ahead — the single richest forward-looking donor channel.

source_name: WBG Finances One – procurement notices dataset
why_relevant: Structured, downloadable dataset of World Bank procurement notices (and the sibling major-contract-awards dataset), queryable by country. Better suited to automated monitoring than the HTML project pages, and enables retrospective analysis of which vendors won Montenegrin financial-sector IT packages.

source_name: World Bank Email Alerts (alerts.worldbank.org) – Montenegro procurement notices
why_relevant: Push channel that delivers new Montenegro procurement notices, project documents and research as they publish; a low-cost way to guarantee no missed notice without high-frequency polling.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro procurement notices (with RSS feed)
why_relevant: UNDP is a frequent implementing partner for EU/IPA and bilateral programmes in Montenegro, procuring hardware, software and consultancy for public institutions (e.g. hardware for the social protection sector). Provides a machine-readable RSS feed scoped to Montenegro — the easiest high-signal donor feed to automate. Awardee names are published in the tenders archive, making it a pointer to the local IT vendor ecosystem.

source_name: UNGM – United Nations Global Marketplace (Montenegro notices)
why_relevant: Aggregates tender notices across 40+ UN organisations, including UNOPS assignments in Montenegro (e.g. rule-of-law project IT equipment, UNOPS-RoLMNE-2025-G-002). Relevant where justice/anti-money-laundering/rule-of-law programmes fund systems that touch financial-sector supervision and reporting.

source_name: Delegacija Evropske unije u Crnoj Gori (EEAS) – pozivi na tender / calls
why_relevant: The EU Delegation manages 200+ EU assistance projects in Montenegro and publishes calls for tender and consultancy notices in both Montenegrin and English (e.g. 'poziv na tender – nabavka konsultantskih usluga'). Direct visibility into IPA-funded technical assistance for financial-sector reform, PFM and supervisory capacity, including implementation timelines.

source_name: Revizorsko tijelo Crne Gore – IPA audit authority
why_relevant: Audits IPA-funded operations in Montenegro. Audit reports name programmes, contracting structures and irregularities, which retrospectively reveals which donor-funded financial-sector contracts actually ran, at what value, and where implementation slipped — useful for validating claimed deadlines.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore – Politika javnih nabavki (gov.me) and wapi.gov.me document store
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance is both the procurement policy owner and a major contracting authority for treasury, tax administration and PFM IT. gov.me articles plus the wapi.gov.me file store hold procurement plans, award decisions (odluka o izboru najpovoljnije ponude) and strategy documents that set multi-year budgets and deadlines for financial-sector systems.

source_name: EIB – Montenegro country page and project procurement rules
why_relevant: EIB (and the EC-led Western Balkans Investment Framework it leads) finances Montenegrin public investment; EIB itself does not run promoter tenders but its project pages disclose loan signatures, amounts and sectors, which predict where national tenders will subsequently be published on CeJN. Its own corporate calls for tender cover advisory services.

source_name: MANS – Mreža za afirmaciju nevladinog sektora (procurement watchdog reporting)
why_relevant: Montenegro's leading anti-corruption NGO systematically investigates public procurement, files FOI requests and publishes analyses naming contracting authorities and winning vendors. Reveals procurement facts that official channels present blandly or omit, and is a pointer to the politically connected slice of the IT vendor ecosystem.
